findings.location: module header vs runtime dispatch wiring; BullMQ stub enable instruction vs config validator; dispatch_job chokepoint
findings.line: queue_adapter.py:10-27 (stale 'NOT WIRED INTO REAL TASK DISPATCH' header claiming QUEUE_BACKEND=rq has no effect), 251-252 (BullMQ docstring 'Enable by setting QUEUE_BACKEND=bullmq'), 267-276 (get_queue_adapter; bullmq branch 274-275 unreachable), 322-364 (dispatch_job chokepoint); call sites api/tasks.py:409,420,431,526,589,599,714,815,850,1113 and main.py:1047; config.py:2082-2084 (validator accepts only asyncio|rq)
findings.finding: The module documentation contradicts runtime wiring in two ways. (a) The header (10-27) still claims every real task-launch call site dispatches via BackgroundTasks.add_task() directly and 'QUEUE_BACKEND=rq currently has no effect on real task dispatch'. That is stale: dispatch_job() (322-364) is the single real chokepoint, is called by all 10 real dispatch sites in api/tasks.py plus the dependency auto-dispatch loop in main.py:1047, and routes QUEUE_BACKEND=rq to a real RQ job (RQAdapterBridge -> RQQueueAdapter with Retry). Git timeline: the 'documented, not wired' note was added 2026-07-27 (b30993fc, ORCH-04-016 fix pass); the real wiring landed 9 days later 2026-08-05 (bda3e9f5) and the note was never updated. (b) The BullMQQueueAdapter class docstring (251-252) says 'Enable by setting QUEUE_BACKEND=bullmq in environment', but the config validator rejects anything outside asyncio|rq (config.py:2082-2084) - the enable path is impossible and get_queue_adapter's bullmq branch (274-275) is unreachable.
findings.evidence: Grep of dispatch_job call sites (10 in api/tasks.py, 1 in main.py); file reads of queue_adapter.py:10-27, 248-264, 267-276, 322-364; git log -S dates (b30993fc 2026-07-27 'Audit 4 done' vs bda3e9f5 2026-08-05 'enhanced' adding 'async def dispatch_job' and the first tasks.py call sites); config.py:2082-2084.
findings.production_impact: Operator-facing only: the docs assert the queue backend is inert when it is live (switching to rq does change the failure model - persistent separate worker process with retries vs in-process BackgroundTasks with a wall-clock bound), and a stub advertises an enable path that configuration validation blocks. No runtime defect; this is the opposite of a missing capability.
findings.confidence: High (call-site grep + git history dates + validator read)
findings.recommendation: Rewrite the module header to describe current behavior (default=BackgroundTasks wrapped in job_wall_clock_timeout_seconds, rq=real Redis Queue via dispatch_job) and cite the current dispatch sites; fix or remove the BullMQ 'enable' sentence and state that the stub is unreachable until the validator and adapter are extended together.

findings.location: memory consolidation archiving write vs retention's designated writer for the naive archived_at column
findings.line: consolidation.py:238-243 (UPDATE memory_embeddings SET archived = true, archived_at = now() at 240); retention.py:44-70 (now_naive = datetime.now(timezone.utc).replace(tzinfo=None) at 53, bound at 58; memory_embeddings via _archive_table at 242); models.py:767 (naive archived_at, migration 022)
findings.finding: memory_embeddings.archived_at (one of only 4 naive DateTime columns in the whole schema, all deliberately naive per migrations 019/022) has two writers with different timezone semantics. retention.py is the designed writer and binds a tz-stripped UTC naive value (now_naive). Memory consolidation additionally archives merged rows with a server-side SQL now() (timestamptz), which Postgres silently casts to the naive column via the session TimeZone. The same column therefore carries values whose implicit timezone depends on which writer archived the row.
findings.evidence: consolidation.py:240 (raw UPDATE with now()); retention.py:53/58 (tz-stripped bind) and 242 (memory_embeddings handled by the same helper); migration 022 introduced the naive archived_at for memory_embeddings; the other three naive columns (task_logs/agent_runs/artifacts.archived_at) have only the retention writer.
findings.production_impact: Interpretation ambiguity for retention/observability reports that read archived_at (consolidated-into-survivor vs aged-out rows carry differently-anchored timestamps); no crash (cast is server-side, no asyncpg bind) and no data loss. Low.
findings.recommendation: Bind archived_at in consolidation.py:240 exactly like retention.py does (datetime.now(timezone.utc).replace(tzinfo=None) passed as :now) so all writers of the four naive archived_at columns share one convention.

findings.line: .env.example:15 ('~85 backend variables'); docs/DEPLOYMENT.md:57 ('96 documented variables as of Audit 06, 2026-07-27'); actual Settings fields and backend/.env.example names both 304; docs/DEPLOYMENT.md:165-166 (S3 appears only in the changelog section)
findings.finding: Deployment-facing documentation carries stale configuration counts: root .env.example advertises '~85 backend variables' and docs/DEPLOYMENT.md says '96 documented variables as of Audit 06, 2026-07-27'; the scripted diff shows Settings (304 fields) and backend/.env.example (304 names) are exactly in sync at 304. In addition DEPLOYMENT.md gives no operational guidance for the two optional services the code fully supports: ARTIFACT_BACKEND=s3 (real S3 upload/retrieval with bucket/IAM requirements) and REDIS_STREAMS_ENABLED=true (stream fan-out + scheduled drain loop) - S3 is only mentioned in the changelog paragraph.
findings.evidence: Scripted Settings<->.env.example diff (304/304, zero differences both directions; 130 active assignments + 174 commented placeholders); the two doc lines above; config.py:879-940 (queue/redis/s3 fields incl. validator coupling); main.py:2012-2036 (health checks for the optional services); store.py/s3_store.py real dual-backend implementation.
findings.production_impact: Doc-only: operators underestimate the configuration surface and lack steps to enable the two real optional services (S3 artifact storage, Redis Streams). No runtime effect.
findings.recommendation: Replace the approximate counts with the exact '304 and in sync' statement (or a one-line diff command), and add short S3 (bucket + IAM/scoping + s3_bucket requirement when artifact_backend=s3) and Redis Streams (enable flag + drain loop note) subsections to docs/DEPLOYMENT.md.

Queue backend switching is real: get_queue_adapter (queue_adapter.py:267-276) returns RQAdapterBridge for rq, BullMQ stub for bullmq, AsyncioQueueAdapter by default; RQAdapterBridge wraps the real RQQueueAdapter (rq_adapter.py:36-145: two named queues, Retry(queue_job_retry_max), 30-min job timeout); BullMQQueueAdapter raises NotImplementedError from enqueue/get_status (254-261) instead of silently no-op-ing; dispatch_job (322-364) is the single chokepoint (10 calls in api/tasks.py + main.py:1047) with the wall-clock bound applied to BOTH backends (290-319; job_wall_clock_timeout_seconds=1800).

Dead-letter handling persists to a queryable table: _write_failed_event INSERTs failed_events rows (bus.py:144-178); for RQ, sweep_failed_rq_jobs (queue_adapter.py:367-445) drains FailedJobRegistry into the same table and is scheduled by a lifespan loop that no-ops unless QUEUE_BACKEND=rq (main.py:330-362, task registered at 1723; interval default 300s).

No double-processing on any event-bus configuration: publish_event persists + pg_notify + fans out to redis_streams.publish_to_stream which no-ops when REDIS_STREAMS_ENABLED=false (redis_streams.py:74-80); the drain loop (main.py:365-391, task at 1730, 60s default) only logs+ACKs and XAUTOCLAIMs stale PEL entries (157-229) - it never re-dispatches business logic; the in-process subscriber registry has zero registered subscribers in production code (documented dormant at redis_streams.py:164-172). get_unprocessed_events has no production caller (dormant capability).

Artifact storage dual-backend reality: default db backend writes local disk ({worktrees_dir}/../artifacts/{uuid}) with asyncio.to_thread wrapping (store.py:165-167 - the old event-loop-blocking bug is fixed), artifacts row with content_sha256 + opportunistic repo_id (187-204); S3 backend is a real gzip implementation with key scheme {s3_key_prefix}{task_id}/{artifact_type}/{artifact_id}.json.gz (s3_store.py:47-84), lazy boto3 client with env/IAM fallback (30-44), real list/delete (119-147); upload failure degrades to disk consistently (store.py:141-148).

Artifact retrieval correctness + security: get_artifact_content (store.py:221-290) dispatches on the STORED storage_path scheme (s3:// -> load_artifact_s3_by_key; else disk) - prior audit's INFRA-06-002 S3-404 fix verified live in code; SHA-256 integrity check logged on mismatch (293-311); both endpoints require require_authenticated (api/artifacts.py:16-48); path traversal infeasible: a live Starlette/TestClient experiment showed ..%2F..%2F... and ..%2f variants do NOT match the {artifact_id} route (404 - encoded slashes are never decoded into the captured param).

not_found: No migration-chain defects found: no gaps, no duplicate revisions, no unresolved down_revision references, no merge points/branch labels (searched via full AST chain walk of all 62 files).

No ORM<->DB drift found: no model field lacking a DDL column and no DDL column lacking a model field on any modelled table (46-table schema reconstructed from upgrades-only; all initial mismatches reconciled to parser blind spots).

No aware-datetime binding into a naive column found anywhere: all raw-SQL aware-datetime binds target timezone=True columns; the only naive columns (4x archived_at) have the tz-stripped retention writer (plus the single inconsistent now() writer = INFRA-06-102).

No S3 stub and no half-finished feature: the S3 path is a full gzip implementation with retrieval-by-stored-key; CI contains no deploy job at all (searched deploy/vercel/render/fly/railway terms - only comments and test fixtures).

Alembic up/down/up migration drill was NOT re-run in this audit (read-only mandate; requires a live DB) - chain integrity fully verified statically instead; prior drill evidence referenced at docs/DEPLOYMENT.md:40-43 + What_is/AUDIT_REPORT/evidence/migration_drills.sh (external artifact).
